name: K.E. on the Track
sources: style-research-extended vol.1 atl-swag-rap — K.E. on the Track
notes: The origin wave's house producer — he built the "futuristic swag" hit template (F.L.Y. "Swag Surfin'", five of nine tracks on Roscoe Dash's *Ready Set Go!*) and then crossed it into pop/R&B. A producer's model is their workflow, and his workflow has one governing rule: **leave the mid-range empty**. The research states it directly — "ringtone-inspired midi loops ... high register, deliberately leaving the mid-range clear for stacked vocal hooks (the records he made with Roscoe Dash are documented as carrying up to '20 Dashes per track')." That is why `melody.register` starts at 74 and `chords.voicing.register` tops out at 72: the two blocks are pushed apart on purpose and the hole between them is where the vocal goes. It is the parameter that distinguishes him inside his own lane. The second is brightness: "the albums he anchors are documented as hip-hop/pop/contemporary-R&B blends, so major and Mixolydian beds with real IV-V motion sit next to static minor vamps" — hence a mixed major/minor family pool, unusual on this axis. Third is the split bass: "mid-decay tuned 808 doubling the root with a separate synth-bass layer above it, rather than one all-purpose sub — the reason his records read on radio and ringtone alike." The 808 stays root-clean and `bassline` is the synth layer, so it is `independent_riff` at `followRootsProb` 0.66 up in [26,45]. ⚠ `confidence` is "low" because the research rates it medium-low and is explicit about why: "no interview establishing his personal drum-programming or harmonic method was reachable, so those lines are era-level inference." INFERRED and marked [LOW-CONF]: the BPM range (68-78 half-time = 136-156), every chord numeral (the I-IV-V and I-V-vi-IV families are the inferred parameter), the 808 split above, and his personal placement habits — the drum block here is Complex's era description ("clap/snare on beat 3, skittering hi-hats in 16ths with triplet inserts, snap-lineage layered claps and tambourine, rolls only as section markers"), not his. ⚠ `hihat.rolls.freqPerBar` is low at 0.24 despite the dense `fillDensity`, because "rolls only as section markers" is the one placement claim the research does source. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 45 to 44 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 45 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 1. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
